full_judgment: 2. Facts of the case briefly stated are that the municipal holding No. 9 at Gopi Kishan Lane, Wari, Dacca originally belonged to one Charu Chandra Guha. The Government requisitioned it including a building thereon by an order dated 16-5-49 under the East Bengal Emergency Requisition of Property Act, 1948 briefly the Requisition Act, for a public purpose. While the house was under requisition the owner, Charu Chandra Guha transferred it to one Abdul Jabbar under a registered deed of exchange dated 16-6-65, Abdul Jabbar, in his turn, entered into an agreement for sale of the holding to the petitioner and received the full consideration of Rs. 1,40,000/00, but Were the transaction was complete he died leaving a widow, four sons and three daughters as his heirs. They adhered to the agreement and executed a registered sale-deed in favour of the petitioner on 6-12-69. The petitioner produced his sale deed before different authorities including respondent No. 1, the Additional Deputy Commissioner and prayed for mutation of his name as owner of the holding in the Record of the Requisition Case. The municipal authorities accepted his claim of ownership and mutated his name in the municipal register. But the Additional Deputy Commissioner refused to mutate the petitioner's name in the register of requisitioned properties whereupon the petitioner filed appeal before the Divisional Commissioner who allowed the appeal and directed Respdt. No. 1, to mutate the petitioner's name. But when no action was taken by Respdt. No. 1 even then, the petitioner filed a suit against Respdt. No. 1 and others in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge. Dacca and while the suit was pending the respondents ci me to terms with the petitioner, accepted his claim of ownership and recorded his name as owner of the holding in the relevant file of the Requisition Case (No. C-942/49). The suit, T.S. No. 72/73 resulted in an exparte decree on 23-9-74. The petitioner then filed an application before the respondents for releasing the property from requisition on the ground that he required it for his own residential purpose. The Government in the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms (Respdt. No. 4) considered the petitioner's application for de-requisition and by an order dated 17-9-73 as already referred to directed that the property be released at once from de-requisition and vacant possession thereof be restored to its legal owner. The petitioner then approached the respondents on several occasions to give effect to this order but no action was taken. In these circumstances the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the rule.
